Strength recovery (plantarflexor strength, often assessed with SLCR or dynamometry) is a key prognostic factor
ROM recovery (ankle dorsiflexion) and functional test performance inform RTS readiness
Sport-specific demands must be considered — RTS criteria should match the loading requirements of the athlete's sport
Return-to-sport activity may begin PRIOR to complete symptom absence — zero-pain is not required
Psychological factors (confidence, fear of re-injury) affect RTS outcomes and should be assessed
No single universally adopted numeric threshold set for RTS — multi-criterion approach is preferred
clinical_question: What prognostic factors determine successful return to sport after midportion Achilles tendinopathy, and what is the evidence for specific return-to-sport criteria?
applicability: Stage 3 Achilles tendinopathy rehabilitation and return-to-sport planning. Supports a multi-domain RTS assessment framework and reinforces that symptom acceptability (not symptom absence) is the appropriate progression standard.

recommended_loading_parameters.notes: Systematic review — not a loading protocol. For RTS planning: assess all six domains (pain, tendon tissue, strength, ROM, function, sport demands) and use sport-specific threshold targets. Begin progressive return-to-participation when criteria are met across domains.

progression_criteria: Return to participation when: (1) pain with target activity ≤3/10 and recovering promptly, (2) plantarflexor strength LSI ≥90%, (3) functional tests LSI ≥90%, (4) ROM comparable to unaffected limb, (5) patient psychologically confident for return. Progress to full competition when all domains reach sport-specific targets.
regression_criteria: Step back from RTS process if any domain deteriorates — particularly if pain with sport-specific activity increases beyond threshold or if functional test LSI drops below 85%.
contraindications: Return to competition is contraindicated without multi-domain assessment. Single-criterion RTS decisions (e.g., pain alone) are not recommended.

criteria.label: Pain with sport-specific activity ≤3/10 and recovering promptly after
criteria.notes: Zero pain is NOT required for RTS. Acceptable pain during sport-specific load is ≤3/10 with prompt recovery.

criteria.label: Plantarflexor strength LSI ≥90% (SLCR or dynamometry)
criteria.notes: Strength recovery is a key prognostic factor. SLCR LSI ≥90% is the minimum standard.

criteria.label: Functional tests (hop battery) LSI ≥90%
criteria.notes: Functional performance symmetry must be confirmed before return to competitive sport.

title: Return-to-Walking and Return-to-Running Program for Achilles Tendinopathy: Criteria-Based Protocol Synthesised from Evidence
authors: Synthesised from: Griffin et al. 2021; Pringels et al. 2025; Corrigan et al. 2022; Habets et al. 2018; Gabbett 2016
summary: Criteria-based return-to-walking and return-to-running protocol for Achilles tendinopathy, synthesised from the highest-quality available evidence. The protocol defines discrete stages: (1) pain-free walking, (2) graded walking load, (3) walk-run intervals, (4) continuous running, (5) sport-specific running. Each stage has explicit entry gates (pain thresholds, functional test benchmarks) and exit criteria. The protocol distinguishes insertional AT (compression-managed positioning, avoid end-range dorsiflexion) from midportion AT (standard loading positions). The 10% weekly load increase rule is the primary load progression constraint throughout.
key_points: Running entry gate: daily activity pain <2/10 at comfortable walking pace (Griffin 2021; Habets 2018)
Running entry gate: VISA-A ≥70 before running reintroduction (Corrigan 2022)
Walking phase: begin on flat terrain, comfortable pace; pain ≤2/10 during and next morning
Walk-run intervals: start 1:4 ratio (1 min run : 4 min walk); pain ≤3/10 to progress
Continuous running entry: pain ≤2/10 at brisk walking pace confirmed for 3 sessions
Running load progression: maximum 10% total volume increase per week (Gabbett 2016)
Speed progression: achieve distance goals before adding speed — never increase both simultaneously
Pain monitoring: use 3-timepoint rule throughout (during, 1hr after, next morning — all <5/10)
Minimum 8 weeks total programme before return to sport running (Pringels 2025)
Maintain heavy strength loading on non-running days throughout all running stages
Insertional AT: use slight plantarflexion bias during walking/running; avoid sudden incline increases
If pain exceeds threshold at any stage: reduce volume 30-40%, do not advance, reassess next session
clinical_question: What are the specific criteria-based stages and thresholds for returning patients with Achilles tendinopathy to walking and running activities?
applicability: Stage 2→3 transition onwards. Applicable to both midportion and insertional AT with noted modifications. Particularly relevant to athletic and recreational running populations. Combine with continued strength loading — do not substitute running for strengthening.

stage_walk_graded.protocol: 20-30 min flat-terrain walking, comfortable pace, daily if tolerated
stage_walk_graded.progression: Add 5 min per session when pain criteria met for 3 consecutive sessions

stage_walk_run_intervals.protocol: 1 min run : 4 min walk, total 20-30 min, 3 times/week
stage_walk_run_intervals.progression: Reduce walk interval by 1 min per week when pain criteria met

stage_continuous_running.protocol: 10-15 min continuous running, flat terrain, conversational pace

stage_return_to_sport_running.entry_gate: 30 min continuous running pain ≤2/10; hop test LSI ≥90%
stage_return_to_sport_running.protocol: Sport-specific drills, progressive intensity, team training reintroduction
stage_return_to_sport_running.pain_ceiling: ≤3/10 during sport-specific activity; recover to baseline within 24hrs
stage_return_to_sport_running.progression: Increase sport-specific load 10%/week; full competition after clinician clearance

progression_criteria: Advance each running stage when: pain at all 3 timepoints (during, 1hr after, next morning) is within stage ceiling AND no week-to-week worsening for 3 consecutive sessions. Never increase distance AND speed simultaneously.
regression_criteria: If pain exceeds ceiling at any timepoint: reduce current stage volume by 30-40% and do not progress for 2 sessions. If pain remains elevated after reduction: regress to previous stage. Return to strength-only loading if running stage cannot be tolerated.
contraindications: Running contraindicated until: daily activity pain <2/10, Stage 2 HSR loading (4×6 at 85% 1RM) tolerated, VISA-A ≥70. High irritability precludes running at all stages.

insertional_at_modifications.positioning: Maintain neutral or slight plantarflexion ankle position; avoid downhill running initially
insertional_at_modifications.footwear: Use moderate heel-to-toe drop shoes (8-12mm) to reduce insertion compression during running
insertional_at_modifications.stretching: Avoid Achilles/calf stretching — compresses insertion. Foam roll calf belly only.
insertional_at_modifications.incline: Avoid uphill/downhill running until Stage 4 running exposure — incline increases insertion compression

criteria.label: Daily activity pain <2/10 (walking, stairs, daily tasks) — running entry gate
criteria.evidence: Griffin et al. 2021; Corrigan et al. 2022
criteria.notes: The single most consistent running entry gate across programs. Patient self-report at clinic review.

criteria.label: VISA-A ≥70 before beginning running reintroduction
criteria.notes: VISA-A <70 contraindicates running. Combined with daily activity pain <2/10 as dual entry gate.

criteria.label: 30 minutes continuous running with pain ≤2/10 for 3 consecutive sessions
criteria.notes: 30-minute pain-free continuous running at conversational pace is the minimum sport-exposure prerequisite.

criteria.label: Minimum 8 weeks total programme before sport-specific running
criteria.notes: Time gate is non-negotiable. 24 sessions at 3×/week = 8 weeks minimum.
